topology: 2 nodes x1 H100, NCCL 2.29.3 GIN (GPU-initiated networking), GDAKI backend, put-ring issued from a device kernel through ncclGin with one signal per put
why: NCCL's OTHER data plane. Case 02 covers NCCL's ordinary traffic, which its proxy thread posts with ibv_post_send and the ibverbs provider records inside the call. GIN is new in NCCL 2.28+ and does not go through that door at all: the GPU builds every WQE in a GPU-resident send queue and the doorbell is rung by whoever the backend chose. This case proves pcomm captures that plane, whole, against the workload's own byte count — the claim case 12 makes for NVSHMEM's IBGDA, made for NCCL.
why_no_goldens: every quantity is allocation- or fabric-dependent: qp_num, which of the node's HCAs a rank lands on, how many doorbells a batch of puts becomes. What survives is the workload's own arithmetic — chunk_bytes x puts_per_iter x iters of payload per rank, and one signal per put — which is what gin_puts_arrived.sql asserts.
platform_note: MN5 only, and for two reasons measured rather than assumed (job 45913525). GIN needs NCCL's INTERNAL net_ib transport: MN5 loads HPC-X's external network plugin by default, which has no GIN backends, so the job sets NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none. And GIN needs symmetric memory, which needs CUDA P2P among local ranks — so this case must NOT disable P2P the way case 12 does for NVSHMEM. du04 runs the workload correctly but pcomm captures nothing of its GDAKI plane (things-to-circle-back-to.md); the case skips where it cannot capture, and only where it cannot.
gin_note: GIN has two backends and they need different doors. GIN_IB_GDAKI (this case) is GPU-initiated: DOCA GPUNetIO builds the queues with DEVX and the doorbell writer depends on the NIC handler — GPU_SM_DB where the driver maps a UAR into the GPU, CPU_PROXY where it does not. On MN5 it is CPU_PROXY, so --enable-host-doorbell is the arm. GIN_IB_PROXY is the other backend: the GPU queues descriptors for a CPU thread which posts them with ibv_post_send, so the ibverbs provider already records it with no new door at all (measured on both hosts: 20,548 writes and 20,480 atomics per rank).
arm_note: NCCL_GIN_GDAKI_NIC_HANDLER=1 pins the handler to CPU_PROXY rather than letting DOCA choose. Pinned, because DOCA's AUTO asks whether the GPU can register the doorbell page and pcomm's host arm has by then substituted a page of ordinary host memory for it — the run measured the same either way on MN5 (auto and pinned both captured the full volume), but a case should not depend on that coincidence holding in the next DOCA version.
workload_note: `gin_putring 128 1024 20`: every iteration each rank fills its send window with a pattern unique to (rank, iteration, word), puts it to its right neighbour's window as 1,024 puts of 128 B from one device kernel — one put per thread, each carrying a GIN signal increment — waits until its own signal has counted every put the left neighbour has made, and checks every word against the neighbour's pattern for that iteration. So the workload fails non-zero if a single byte is missing, stale or duplicated, and 'OK' is a claim rather than a print statement. Exit 4 means this communicator has no GIN, which is the only skip.
negative_control: The job runs the same workload passively first (no doorbell arm) and asserts the capture has NO mlx5_device_send rows. Measured on MN5: passive sees 166 DEVX queues and not one send, so 'the door captured it' and 'the traffic was there anyway' stay distinguishable — the same control case 12 runs for the same reason.
oracle_note: The workload's own arithmetic is the oracle, and it is independent of pcomm: 128 B x 1,024 puts x 20 iters = 2,621,440 B of payload per rank, and 20,480 signal atomics of 8 B. Measured exactly, on both ranks, MN5 job 45913525.
queue_depth_note: GDAKI's send queue is 128 slots by default (NCCL_GIN_GDAKI_QP_DEPTH), eight times shallower than NVSHMEM's 1,024 — and it does not matter here, which is the whole difference between this door and the send-queue watcher. The host doorbell copies the queue BEFORE forwarding the doorbell, so the NIC cannot consume and the GPU cannot recycle a slot before pcomm has read it; the watcher is passive and nobody waits for it, which is why case 11 must set NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH=8192 and this case sets nothing. Measured, MN5 job 45913713, every run wqes_lapped=0 and every byte exact: depth 128 with 1,024 puts x 20 iters, with 4,096 puts x 50 iters (409,600 WQEs/rank), and with 8,192 puts of 8 B x 50 iters (819,200 WQEs/rank); depths 1,024 and 8,192 changed nothing but the batching (61 to 24,426 doorbells for identical traffic, which is the instrument moving what it measures — do not read WQEs-per-doorbell off an armed capture as a property of the application).
